title: Injective on cohomology of the principal-open Cech augmentation
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $X=\operatorname{Spec}(A)$ [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, $f:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to A$, $V=\bigcup_iD(f_i)$ and $D_S=D(\prod_{j\in S}f_j)$. Let $J$ be an arbitrary unbounded K-injective cochain complex of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let $K,T$ be complexes of $A$-modules, with degreewise $A$-linear isomorphisms $\sigma_n:K^n\cong\Gamma(V,J^n)$ and $\tau_n:T^n\cong\prod_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq\operatorname{Fin}(r)}\Gamma(D_S,J^{n+1-|S|})$. Assume $\sigma$ identifies the differential of $K$ with the sectionwise differential of $J$, and $\tau$ identifies the differential of $T$ with the signed total formula: at $S$ its vertical term is $(-1)^{|S|-1}d_J$ and its horizontal term is the sum over $j\in S$ of restriction from $D_{S\setminus\{j\}}$, multiplied by $(-1)^{|\{i\in S:i<j\}|}$, with empty deletions zero. All coefficient degrees are transported by their displayed integer equalities. Let $\alpha:K\to T$ be a chain map which under these coordinates is restriction from $V$ on singleton coordinates and zero on all larger subsets. The open inclusion inequalities and degree equalities in the Lean signature specify only the transports in these formulas. Then $H^n(\alpha)$ is injective for every $n\in\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Replace J by a degreewise-injective functorial K-injective resolution I. The quasi-isomorphism between the two K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence. Its sectionwise maps induce homotopy equivalences on K and T: in Cech degree p apply the coefficient homotopy with sign (-1)^p. Naturality of restrictions cancels the horizontal terms and the vertical signs multiply to one. Augmentation naturality follows from the coordinate formulas. These statements use the same finite-total homotopy calculation as the tuple model, reindexed by the unique increasing enumeration of each subset.

Every augmented section row of I over the cover of V is exact. Injective modules are flasque, hence remain Cech-acyclic on any open; sheaf gluing identifies the degree-zero kernel with sections over V and gives injectivity of augmentation. Ordered-to-increasing Cech comparison gives alternating row exactness; identify increasing tuples with nonempty finite subsets, and their face positions with the subset deletion signs. The augmented columns run only from -1 through r-1.

For a closed section whose image is the differential of a total cochain, kill the highest Cech column of the cochain by subtracting a total boundary, using row exactness. Its differential is unchanged. Repeat down to column zero; exactness there expresses the remaining cochain as the augmentation of a section. The injectivity of the row augmentation shows the original closed section is the vertical differential of that section, so its class was zero. This finite staircase never requires boundedness in the coefficient degree. For r=0, V is empty and the sheaf axiom makes its section modules zero, while the target product has no indices.

Transfer injective of the homology map from I to J through the augmentation naturality square, whose other sides are homotopy equivalences and hence induce isomorphisms on cohomology. Degreewise coordinate isomorphisms identify these maps with the displayed alpha.
